cvEn:
Sergei Guntmacher, son of Ella and Isaak, was born on 22 Kislev 5747 (24 December 1986) in Ukraine. He is the brother of Galina, Anastasia, Ilya and Alexei.

He was married to Marina and was the father of Roy and Tal.

When Sergei was seven, his father passed away. In 2001 he immigrated to Israel together with his mother and brothers, and they settled in Ramat Gan.

He studied at the ORT Pardes Hanna agricultural high school and completed his studies in 2004.

After his studies he enlisted in the army and served as a combat soldier in the Givati Brigade.

During his service he took part in the "Netiv" course (designed to strengthen Jewish identity in preparation for conversion within the army framework), where he met Marina, who was also a soldier. The two became a couple.

After their discharge from the army they married, and two children were born to them: their son Roy and their daughter Tal. Having grown up from a young age without a father, it was important to him to give his children what he had been denied as a child: play, laughter, endless patience alongside energy and mischief. Fatherhood brought him great joy, and his wife described him as a "super-dad."

Besides being a devoted family man, he loved sports such as CrossFit, weightlifting and running. An avid skier, he made a point of skiing with his family every year.

His character was that of a dominant, caring and devoted person, who was a listening ear for everyone around him, and he also had an excellent sense of humor. A childhood friend said he was "an amazing guy, with a heart of gold. One of the best people I have known. He was always funny, always going along with the silliness; every moment in his company was fun."

Sergei worked for many years in the security field. From 2013 to 2020 he worked at the Ministry of Culture and Sport in the Department of Security, Emergency and Cyber, guarding Minister Miki Zohar's predecessor, Minister Akunis, and advanced to the position of shift manager in the Tel Aviv district. Ministry staff said he was pleasant-mannered, very wise, liked and loved by the office staff and those around him, and radiated calm. They added that he shared stories about his family and his children, whom he loved so much. A colleague described him as "a rare guy, diligent, with knowledge and constant giving."

In 2020 Sergei changed his career path and began working as an independent financial and pension agent. He invested effort in learning the field, passed the Capital Market Authority examinations, and received his professional license as an insurance agent two weeks before he fell.

In 2023 he was hired by an insurance agency. At his new workplace, "Rimonim Investments and Holdings Ltd.," they were already expecting him after the Tishrei holidays of 5784; he was photographed for the agency's website, and a new company car was already parked in his home parking space.

On Shabbat, 22 Tishrei, Simchat Torah 5784, 7 October 2023, at half past six in the morning, the terrorist organization Hamas launched a surprise attack on Israel. Under cover of massive rocket and missile fire from the Gaza Strip into wide areas of the country, thousands of terrorists infiltrated by land, sea and air, and began a murderous assault on the communities of the Gaza envelope and on Sderot, Ofakim and Netivot, on the Nova music festival near the kibbutzim Re'im and Nir Oz, on IDF bases and on travelers on the roads in the area. The terrorists murdered some eight hundred civilians in their homes and in their cars, after committing severe atrocities against them. They abducted hundreds of Israelis to the Gaza Strip and destroyed, looted and set fire to homes and property. Hundreds of soldiers, police officers, security personnel and members of local emergency squads fell in battle. That morning, the war began.

At 10:30 that morning, even before receiving an official Tzav 8 call-up order, Sergei reported for reserve duty and set out with determination to defend the country. A friend of his said: "You fought in every operation here since you were drafted into Givati. Even when Roy and Tal were born, you always showed up. Also in this war, on 7.10, you packed your bag together with Marina and set out. You always said you believed in the importance of every operation and there was no chance you wouldn't go. This time too. What a hero you are."

During the war he served as a combat soldier in the 8208th Battalion of the 261st Brigade, and a fellow fighter testified that in the hard moments he put a smile on everyone's face and made them laugh.

On 22 January 2024, Sergei went out with his battalion on a ground operation in the Al-Maghazi refugee camp in the southern Gaza Strip. During the operation twenty-one soldiers were killed, Sergei among them.

Master Sergeant Sergei Guntmacher fell in battle on 12 Shevat 5784 (22 January 2024), aged thirty-seven. He was laid to rest in the military cemetery in Petah Tikva. He is survived by his wife, a son and a daughter, his mother, two sisters and two brothers.

His sister wrote: "Our world shattered on the day you fell, when men in uniform knocked on our door... To say that we will not forget you is like saying that we love you; that is obvious. You are in our hearts."

As part of Ramat Gan Municipality's memorial project, "In Our Hearts Forever," a memorial film was produced for Sergei: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tthlEYHfd8k.

Sergei is commemorated on the "Memories +" website.
